{{Top|leg|notoc=1}}
{{Quote|You know, I don't think I ever heard how Chiss families are set up. Especially those who make up the Ruling Families.''"<br />''"The Nine Ruling Families are like any other families. Blood and merit create siblings and cousins and ranking distants. Some are released, others are rematched, others are born to trial. The same as any other family.|[[Dean Jinzler]] and [[Aide/Legends|Aide]] [[Chaf'ees'aklaio]]|<ref name="Survivor's Quest">''[[Survivor's Quest]]''</ref>}}
'''Chiss families''' were a social unit of the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. The families were made up of a hierarchy of family ranks,<ref name="Survivor's Quest" /> which included from least to greatest, the [[Merit adoptive/Legends|merit adoptive]], [[Trial-born/Legends|trial-born]], and [[Ranking distant/Legends|ranking distant]],<ref name="Outbound Flight">[[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']]</ref> [[Cousin/Legends|cousin]], and [[Sibling (Chiss)|sibling]].<ref name="Survivor's Quest" /> A family rank of [[shadow child]] also existed, which kept an individual with that rank completely secret, to prevent the complete extermination of a Chiss family by their enemies.<ref name="The Joiner King">''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]''</ref> Individuals of the family could be considered senior members, as was the case with [[Aristocra/Legends|Aristocra]] [[Chaf'orm'bintrano]], [[Core name/Legends|core name]] "Formbi," of the [[Chaf family/Legends|Fifth Ruling Family]]<ref name="Survivor's Quest" /> in [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]].<ref name="Survivor's Quest date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Survivor's Quest]]'' to [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]].</ref> In the other case, [[Aide/Legends|Aide]] [[Chaf'ees'aklaio]], core name "Feesa," was too young to be considered a senior member of the Ruling Family.<ref name="Survivor's Quest" />

A Chiss individual belonging to one family could be [[Rematching/Legends|rematched]] to another. In some cases, an individual could also be released to their original family.<ref name="Outbound Flight" /> Members of the [[Chiss Defense Fleet]] were recruited from every Chiss family, which was signified by the [[Color/Legends|black]] [[Defense Fleet uniform]]s.<ref name="Survivor's Quest" /> Upon promotion to a [[Senior officer/Legends|senior officer]] in the Defense Fleet, a [[Chiss officer/Legends|Chiss officer]] was stripped of family name and privilege and made part of the [[Defense Hierarchy]] in order that they may serve all Chiss without deference or prejudice.<ref name="Outbound Flight" />

According to a study in ''[[The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life]]'', the [[Csapla family|Csapla]], [[Nuruodo family|Nuruodo]], [[Inrokini family|Inrokini]] and [[Sabosen family|Sabosen families]] represented bloodlines said to have predated modern Chiss civilization. Every Chiss claimed affiliation with one of the four families, determined by both tradition and place of birth. In reality, these family names were more of a cultural holdover: the bloodlines had grown so co-meddled that any Chiss could claim affiliation to any of the four families.<ref name="The Chiss">{{GamerCite|5|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Chiss}}</ref>
